edit.description.md:
Today the scrubber's series select narrows the board by exactly one axis: the plotted view picks it (tags / assignees / comment authors) and `only` is a single flat id list. Picking a second axis throws the first away, so "assigned to jola AND tagged bug" cannot be expressed.

Make the narrowing per-axis and conjunctive:

- `BoardSelection.only` becomes a per-axis map, not one list. Absent axis = not narrowed.
- `buildBoardFilter` returns every narrowed axis; a ticket has to pass all of them.
- URL and localStorage carry the per-axis shape; a bare legacy `only=` list still reads onto the plotted view's axis.
- In the popover, a row's caret opens that axis's list without changing what the chart plots. The radio still picks the plotted view; ticking any list filters the board.

The chart still colours by one axis at a time — that rule is unchanged.

edit.description.md:
The board can be narrowed to a tag, to an assignee, or to the author of a comment. There is no way to ask "which tickets did claude/peter touch" — the actor behind every other kind of event is not a filter axis.

Add a `People` view to the board series select: it plots every event, like `Board events`, but colours by the event's actor, and its identity list is a fourth filter axis.

add.issue.name: A needle drag commits the position of the last render, not the release

edit.description.md:
`endDrag` in TimeScrubber reads `dragFraction` and `rangeDrag` out of React state. Pointer moves during a drag arrive faster than React commits, so the handler closes over a stale fraction: the forced dispatch on release asks for wherever the last *rendered* move was, not where the pointer let go.

Moves are throttled at 120ms and dispatch the event's own fraction, so under load the throttle can already have asked for a later moment than the release then asks for. The board ends up parked behind the release, and the same staleness shortens a range drag's zoom window.

Found by `scrub-dispatch.pw.ts › dragging the needle commits the position it ends on`, which fails whenever a render is slow enough — reproducible 4/4 with `--repeat-each=4 --workers=4`, and it has taken the pre-push gate down twice.

Fix: hold the live fraction and range in refs written by the pointer handlers, and have `endDrag` read those rather than the state it renders from.

add.issue.name: The TUI comments test walks the detail rows on a timer and can overshoot

edit.description.md:
`comments.e2e.test.ts › wraps a long comment onto more rows` presses ARROW_DOWN up to six times with a 150ms sleep between, breaking when the cursor reaches Comments. Under the pre-push gate's load the render lags past 150ms, every check reads a stale frame, all six presses go through, and the cursor wraps the six detail rows right back to Description — after which the wait for `❯ Comments (1)` can only time out.

Fix: confirm each press before the next, waiting for the row it lands on, rather than sleeping and hoping.

Took the pre-push gate down once; passes on its own in the container.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: two causes, both in commit 9a903979.

The staleness was real — `endDrag` now reads the live fraction and range out of refs the pointer handlers write, not the state it renders from.

But the flake had a second, larger cause the ticket missed: the window itself moved mid-drag. Scrubbing broadcasts, the broadcast fetches a fresh window, and adopting it re-derived the axis under the pointer — so the same fraction stood for a different moment before and after, and the drag's own requests came out unordered. A window that arrives while the pointer is down is now held back and adopted on the release re-render instead.

The test also had to stop comparing the drag against the click that set the needle up: that click is on the pre-scrub window, so its moment is not on the same scale. It waits for the needle to settle before grabbing it, too — the first scrub re-places it, and pressing on the old position drags out a range instead. Now 40/40 green at `--repeat-each=8 --workers=6`, having been 4/4 red before the fix.

add.issue.name: The People filter is window-scoped, and unticking one name reads smaller than it acts

edit.description.md:
The `actor` axis added in WP93ATF is the only one resolved against the scrubber's window rather than board state at the needle — nothing but the event log knows who touched what. Two consequences that need a decision.

The list is a positive one, like every other axis: unticking one person means "show the tickets the remaining people touched", not "hide that person's". Combined with the window scoping, unticking a single name under scope=week drops every ticket nobody touched that week, not just the ones that person touched. The gesture reads as "take their dots off the chart".

The options, none free:

1. Leave it. It answers the question the axis was added for — "which tickets did X touch" — and it is consistent with how the tag and assignee lists already behave. The surprise is real but the semantics are honest.
2. Make it a negative test: a ticket passes unless the window says only unticked people touched it. Unticking one name then does what it looks like — but "show only X" stops narrowing to X's tickets, which is the case the axis exists for.
3. Say the coupling out loud in the UI — a note on the People list that it reads the window, so the scope buttons are visibly part of the answer.
4. Split it in two: a colouring-only People series, and a separate explicit "touched by" filter.

Not blocking the PR: today's behaviour serves the ask it was written for. Filed because which of these is right is a product call, not a code one.

Raised by the review of PR #255.

add.issue.comment.md: Review of the branch caught a hole the fix itself opened: `endDrag` cleared only the ref for the branch it took, and two pointers can leave both a range and a needle drag set. A ref left behind now reads as a gesture still in flight, which — since the window adoption is gated on that — would latch the chart shut for good rather than merely parking the thumb. Both refs and both states are released up front now, before deciding what the gesture was.

The review also raised the axis's window coupling as a usability trap: unticking one name means "show the tickets the rest touched", and against a week-scoped window that drops every ticket nobody touched that week. add.issue.name: The series popover is a radiogroup, but the filter underneath it is not

edit.description.md:
Since 7TN11YK the board narrows on four axes at once — a tag and an assignee hold together. The popover still draws its top-level rows as radios, so the control says "pick exactly one" while the thing underneath it does the opposite. Nothing on screen says a second axis is even possible, and a row narrowed while another is plotted shows only a lit caret.

Make the rows checkboxes, tri-state:

```
[*] Tags
[ ] Comments
[-] Contributors
        [*] claude/agentX
        [ ] claude/agentY
        [*] claude/agentZ
```

- unticked — the axis takes no part in the filter
- ticked — the axis is on with every identity, so a ticket has to carry one of them (assigned to somebody, tagged with something, touched by somebody)
- dash — on with some, the state a partly-ticked child list puts the parent in

Several may be on at once and a ticket has to pass them all, which is what "every tag, for these two contributors" means.

The narrowing already carries this shape; what changes is that an axis present with every id stops collapsing to "not narrowed", and unticking the last child turns the parent off rather than leaving an axis nothing can pass.

**What the chart plots is derived rather than picked.** The single-view radio goes: when exactly one axis is on the chart draws and colours by it, exactly as selecting that view does today; with none or several on it draws every kind and colours by kind, as `Board events` does. Every picture reachable now is still reachable, and the popover stops asking two questions through one control.

The fork, if this is wrong: the top-level rows could instead keep meaning "what the chart plots" and gain multi-select there, with filtering staying implicit. Said out loud in a comment rather than settled quietly.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: commit dad41127.

The rows are `Checkbox`es now, tri-state — `Checkbox` grew a `mixed` prop drawn as a bar and reported as `aria-checked="mixed"`. `Board events` and `Tickets` are gone from the list: neither is a filter axis, so the popover lists exactly the four that are, and the trigger still reads `Board events` when nothing narrows.

The narrowing carries the third state: an axis is absent (off), `'all'` (on with everything, so a ticket has to carry something on it), or a list. `only=assignee:*` in the URL is the middle one. An axis narrowed to nothing normalises to off — that is not a state any checkbox can say, and it left the board unrecoverable.

Clicking a parent replaces the axis outright, never keeping what the children said: on with everything, or off. Covered both ways, in `board-selection.test.ts` for the model and end to end for the round trip out of a half-ticked list.

**`view` left the selection.** What the chart plots is read off the filter — one axis on and the chart is that axis, in its identities' colours, exactly as picking that series used to do; none or several on and it draws every kind. `view=` is no longer written to the URL, only read, and only to place an unprefixed `only` list from a link written before this.

One capability went with it: `Tickets` was a plottable series and is not an axis, so "draw only ticket events" has no control any more. Nothing else changed shape — every other picture reachable before is still reachable.

add.issue.name: A running command looks exactly like one that was never submitted

edit.description.md:
`onConfirmCommandLineSequenceInput` sets `commandIsPending`, awaits the command's action, and only clears the line once it resolves. For the whole of that window the command line still shows the composed text under the `<ENTER> to confirm` hint — the same thing it shows before Enter is pressed at all.

`commandIsPending` reaches `CommandLine.tsx` but is read for one thing only: whether a validation message paints red. Nothing says the command is running.

So a command that takes a moment — a config write against a busy disk, anything doing git work, a sync — reads as a keystroke that never landed. The obvious response is to press Enter again.

Found while pinning down a flaking e2e: the captured frame showed `:config username test  <ENTER> to confirm` three seconds after Enter, and the honest first reading was "the Enter was dropped". It was not; the command was still running. If it misleads someone reading a captured frame, it misleads a user watching the screen.

A spinner, a dimmed line, or the hint swapped for "running…" would each do. The state is already there.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: commit 143fa246. The colon walks while the command runs.

```
idle      : init  <ENTER> to confirm
running   ⠃init      ⠆init      ⠰init      ⠘init
```

Two braille dots — the colon itself — circling the corners of one cell at 120ms, the same register as the sync badge's drift rather than a spinner shouting over the board. One column wide, so nothing on the line moves under it, and the timer only exists while something is pending.

The `<ENTER> to confirm` hint goes while it runs. It is an instruction, and once the command is away it is the wrong one — pressing Enter again is exactly what the missing feedback provokes. Every other message stays: a failure arrives while pending is still true.

The decision is a pure function in `command-line-sigil.ts` with its own test, rather than something only reachable by rendering the component.

Worth recording, because a unit test alone would have shipped it broken: the first cut compared `infoMessage === CONFIRM_MSG` and never matched, because `hintDefault` paints the message and the string arrives wrapped in dim escape codes. Six green tests, and the hint still sat there on screen. Driving the real TUI through a pty is what showed it; the fix matches on the message instead, and the test now feeds it the styled form.

add.issue.name: Event actors are shown under their log file name, so one person reads two ways

edit.description.md:
A contributor shows as `claude-adolph` where they authored an event and `claude/adolph` where they are assigned. The slash is the real name; the dashed form is the storage encoding leaking into the interface.

Nothing carries the name on an event — `stripActor` takes it off before persisting — so `event.userName` is reconstructed by `parseEventFileActor` from the log's own file name, which `sanitizeFilePart` lowercased and stripped to `[a-z0-9._-]`. Its own doc says so: "Lossy on purpose: this is a storage encoding, never a display value... display names come from the contributor registry."

Two readers use it as a display value anyway:

- `timeline-index.ts`, `identitiesFor` — the actor is built straight from `event.userName`, while `tag` and `assignee` beside it go through `identityFor` and the name index. This is what the GUI's Contributors filter, the dot hints and the event log all read.
- `issues.ts`, `getIssueHistory` — the same, for a ticket's Log tab.

The colour goes with it: `getStringColor(event.userName)` hashes the dashed form, so the same person is one colour as an actor and another as an assignee.

`contributors.ts` already does this correctly — `mergeRegistryNames` lets the registry win and keeps the log's copy only for an id the registry has never seen. Both readers above want the same rule, and `buildNameIndex` in `timeline-index.ts` already indexes `create.contributor`, so the name is to hand.

Names written before renames were events still fall back to the file-name form, which is why the fallback stays rather than showing a raw ULID.

add.issue.comment.md:
Correction to the description: **only one reader was affected, not two.** The actor in `timeline-index.ts` now goes through the same name index the tag and the assignee go through, with the file's copy kept as the fallback for an id the log never named.

`getIssueHistory` was already right, and I nearly shipped a no-op "fixing" it. It reads `issue.log` off the materialized state, where the name survives; only the timeline reads events straight out of `loadMergedEvents`, where the name has been round-tripped through the file name. Proved by writing the raw `event.userName` out from inside the running server rather than by reading the code twice — it said `claude/tester`, not `claude-tester`.

Worth recording, because it nearly went the other way: the first attempt to verify the revert was red passed, and the reason was that the reverted file did not compile (an unused helper), so `dist` still held the fix and the browser suite was testing stale output. A "verified red" against a build whose exit code went unread is worth nothing.

The GUI fixture seeded its user as `test`, which has no slash and so could not tell the two spellings apart. It is `claude/tester` now, which makes the whole browser suite able to see this class of bug, and the Contributors list has a test asserting the slashed name is what reaches the screen — red against the old code, green against the new. `issue-history.pw.ts` gained the same assertion on the Log tab; that one guards a path that was already correct.

Commit a9d19313.

Decided by the user, and it is none of the four options — a fifth that dissolves the problem rather than trading one surprise for another: **give every axis a "none" row.**

add.issue.comment.md:
Amended by the user, and they are right: **the contributors axis gets no none row.** Every ticket was created by somebody, so "untouched" is never true of one.
